summary_rationale: India Glycols Limited (INDIAGLYCO) is a complex restructuring story transitioning from a leveraged agro-chemical and liquor conglomerate into a focused, lower-leverage Bio-based Specialties & Performance Chemicals (BSPC) and Industrial Gases platform anchored by a 49% equity stake in Clariant IGL Specialty Chemicals. The apparent 66%–67% YoY revenue collapse in Q1 FY27 (₹357 Cr) and Q2 FY27 (₹362 Cr) is an accounting boundary reset rather than operational distress: under the NCLT-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement (Appointed Date April 1, 2026; Effective Date September 1, 2026), the high-margin Potable Spirits & Bio-Fuels undertaking (IGL Spirits Ltd) and the Nutraceuticals/Bio-Polymers undertaking (Ennature Bio Pharma Ltd) were demerged into standalone entities, removing roughly two-thirds of FY26's ₹4,211 Cr revenue base while also slashing consolidated borrowings from ₹1,691 Cr (March 2026) to ₹826 Cr (September 2026) and quarterly interest expense from ₹45–49 Cr to ₹12 Cr. Operationally, the retained BSPC business possesses genuine green-chemistry differentiation (world's pioneer in molasses/grain-route bio-MEG and bio-EO derivatives) and steady profit/dividend upstreaming from the 49% Clariant JV. However, it earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (not COMPOUNDER_PASS) verdict and PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health because: (1) standalone continuing-operations OPM compressed to 11% in Q1–Q2 FY27 once the ~21% EBIT-margin Potable Spirits engine exited; (2) consolidated 3-year ROE averaged a modest 10.4% (11.3% latest) with negative free cash flow across FY22–FY26 (-₹47 Cr in FY26, -₹391 Cr in FY25) due to heavy capex; and (3) bio-MEG pricing remains structurally tethered to crude-oil-derived petrochemical MEG spreads, exposing margins to feedstock (molasses/grain) vs. crude volatility.
